Section1.That the Governing Body of the City of Cheyenne finds that the text amendment
that is the subject of this ordinance meets the criteria specified in Section 2.4.1.d of the UDC.
Section 2.That the intent of this text amendment is to remove the UDC text specifying a
125 percent maximum parking allowed per site under any circumstance and to allow Applicants
to request the Director of Planning and Development to grant additional parking without
exhausting all options for Parking Credits or Shared Parking, if applicable, conditioned on the
Applicant demonstrating, via a parking study, the need for additional parking and the Applicant
providing two or more of the mitigation measures of Section 6.2.7, subsections a through d.
Section 3. That the intent of this text amendment is to facilitate the redevelopment of infill
properties or to accommodate the special parking needs of new development by allowing
Applicants to seek and justify parking in excess of the Section 6.2.4 requirements, provided that
the Applicant incorporates two or more of the mitigating design features stated in Section 6.2.7.a
through d.
Section 4. That this text amendment is not regarding a specific parcel or a change in
boundary due to a specific development proposal, changed circumstances for any specific property
or its surrounding area, or changed public policy with respect to long-range plans.

This memo pertains to the proposed UDC text amendment to amend Section 6.2.7of the Unified
Development Code, which governs maximum parking for development projects.
Currently, the UDC states that"No site shall be permitted to provide more than 125% of the
public streets.
As stated in Planner Montana's staff report to Planning Commission, City Council, and the Public
Services Committee (all earlier this month), this proposed amendment seeks to“facilitate
development of infill properties that may have been designed and built with large amounts of
parking".Examples of this type of redevelopment are the re-use of former department stores
and shopping centers for churches, offices ora mixof office and retail uses."
The following properties have emerged as those likely to be accommodated by this proposed
amendmentto theUDC's maximum parking policy:
